alt.en: An old sepia photograph looking down on a river curving between wooded banks towards a single high stone arch bridge, with a footpath and small trees on the left bank and thick trees beyond; faint white letters at the foot read "AULD BRIG O' DOON. AYR. 591. J.V."
alt.es: Antigua fotografía en sepia que mira desde lo alto un río que se curva entre orillas arboladas hacia un puente de piedra de un solo arco alto, con un sendero y árboles pequeños en la orilla izquierda y árboles espesos al fondo; al pie, unas letras blancas tenues dicen "AULD BRIG O' DOON. AYR. 591. J.V."

caption.en: The river Doon at Alloway in Ayrshire, near where Burns was born, with the old bridge over it, the Auld Brig o' Doon, in a photograph of about 1875 to 1885: the banks and braes the song's singer walks by.
caption.es: El río Doon en Alloway, en Ayrshire, cerca de donde nació Burns, con su puente antiguo, el Auld Brig o' Doon, en una fotografía de hacia 1875 a 1885: las orillas y laderas junto a las que pasea quien canta la canción.

source: Burns monument te Alloway en Brig o' Doon (Burns Monument at Alloway and Brig o' Doon), album leaf with two albumen prints, photographer anonymous; the lower print, "Auld Brig", numbered "591, J.V." in the negative
licenceEvidence: Rijksmuseum record https://id.rijksmuseum.nl/200728874: rights https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/ (Public Domain Mark 1.0); photographer anonymous, dated ca. 1875 to ca. 1885. Albumen print over 140 years old; anonymous work, 70 years from making long ended. Only the lower print of the leaf is used (see rights.md).

alt.en: An engraved page of music numbered 387, headed "The Banks o' Doon" and "Written for this Work by Robert Burns.", number 374, marked "Slow & tender", with five systems of voice and bass and the words from "Ye Banks and braes o' bonie Doon" to "Departed never to return" under the notes, and the second verse, "Oft hae I rov'd by bonie Doon", printed below, signed B.
alt.es: Página de música grabada con el número 387, con el encabezado "The Banks o' Doon" y "Written for this Work by Robert Burns.", número 374, marcada "Slow & tender", con cinco sistemas de voz y bajo y la letra desde "Ye Banks and braes o' bonie Doon" hasta "Departed never to return" bajo las notas, y la segunda estrofa, "Oft hae I rov'd by bonie Doon", impresa debajo, firmada B.

caption.en: The Banks o' Doon, No. 374 on page 387 of the fourth volume of The Scots Musical Museum, marked "Slow & tender": the song's earliest known printing (Edinburgh, 1792), here in the volume's 1839 Edinburgh reissue, which added the line "Written for this Work by Robert Burns." under the title.
caption.es: The Banks o' Doon, el n.º 374 en la página 387 del cuarto volumen de The Scots Musical Museum, marcado "Slow & tender": la primera impresión conocida de la canción (Edimburgo, 1792), aquí en la reedición del volumen hecha en Edimburgo en 1839, que añadió la línea "Written for this Work by Robert Burns." bajo el título.

source: The Scotish Musical Museum, vol. 4 (Edinburgh: William Blackwood and Sons, 1839), originally published by James Johnson in 1792; p. 387, No. 374, "The Banks o' Doon"
library: University of Western Ontario (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Engraved page first issued 1792, this printing Edinburgh 1839; Burns died 1796, Stephen Clarke 1797, James Johnson 1811, the 1839 editors Stenhouse 1827, Sharpe 1851, Laing 1878 (item record). The Internet Archive record states no licence or restriction. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: University of Western Ontario, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: An engraved title page in flourished script and display letters: "A Second Collection of Strathspey Reels &c. With a Bass for the Violoncello or Harpsichord. Dedicated (By Permission) to the Noblemen & Gentlemen of the Caledonian Hunt, By Neil Gow, at Dunkeld", "Price 6s", with the London seller's line at the foot.
alt.es: Portada grabada con letra caligráfica de rasgos y letras de adorno: "A Second Collection of Strathspey Reels &c. With a Bass for the Violoncello or Harpsichord. Dedicated (By Permission) to the Noblemen & Gentlemen of the Caledonian Hunt, By Neil Gow, at Dunkeld", "Price 6s", con la línea del vendedor de Londres al pie.

caption.en: The title page of Niel Gow's Second Collection of Strathspey Reels, the book that holds the tune's earliest known printing, dedicated to "the Noblemen & Gentlemen of the Caledonian Hunt", to whom Burns had dedicated his Edinburgh edition of 1787; this is a later London issue sold by W. Boag.
caption.es: La portada de la Second Collection of Strathspey Reels de Niel Gow, el libro que contiene la primera impresión conocida de la melodía, dedicado a "the Noblemen & Gentlemen of the Caledonian Hunt", a quienes Burns había dedicado su edición de Edimburgo de 1787; es una edición posterior de Londres, vendida por W. Boag.

source: Niel Gow, A Second Collection of Strathspey Reels &c. with a Bass for the Violoncello or Harpsichord (first published 1788; this issue London: printed and sold by W. Boag, No. 11 Great Turnstile, Lincoln's Inn Fields, undated, catalogued 1795), title page; bound with Gow's first and third collections
library: University of Western Ontario (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Engraved title page, first published 1788, this London issue undated (catalogued 1795; it offers Gow's Third Collection of 1792); Niel Gow died 1807 (item record: "Gow, Niel, 1727-1807"); engraver and publisher of the 1790s long dead. The Internet Archive record states no licence or restriction. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
credit: University of Western Ontario, via the Internet Archive

alt.en: The top of an engraved page of music numbered 1, headed "The Caledonian Hunts Delight." and "A favorite Air", marked Slow, with two systems of treble and bass in 6/8 with trill signs, and no words.
alt.es: La parte superior de una página de música grabada con el número 1, con el encabezado "The Caledonian Hunts Delight." y "A favorite Air", marcada Slow, con dos sistemas de clave de sol y de fa en 6/8 con signos de trino, y sin letra.

caption.en: The Caledonian Hunt's Delight, "A favorite Air" marked Slow, on page 1 of Gow's Second Collection, the book of the tune's earliest known printing (Dick and Glen date it 1788), a few years before the Museum printed the tune with Burns's words; this page is from the later London issue.
caption.es: The Caledonian Hunt's Delight, "A favorite Air" marcada Slow, en la página 1 de la Second Collection de Gow, el libro de la primera impresión conocida de la melodía (Dick y Glen lo fechan en 1788), pocos años antes de que el Museum la imprimiera con la letra de Burns; esta página es de la edición posterior de Londres.

source: Niel Gow, A Second Collection of Strathspey Reels &c. (first published 1788; this issue London: W. Boag, undated, catalogued 1795), p. 1, "The Caledonian Hunts Delight. A favorite Air" (top of the page only)
library: University of Western Ontario (digitized by the Internet Archive)
licenceEvidence: Engraved page, first published 1788, this London issue undated (catalogued 1795); Niel Gow died 1807; the tune's makers, James Miller and Stephen Clarke (died 1797), worked in the 1780s. The Internet Archive record states no licence or restriction. Faithful scan of a flat page adds no new copyright (see rights.md).
